title: Zero-hour spotters notebook
content:
TL;DR: Quiet night but two recurring things to watch: (1) intermittent kv-cache eviction storms causing 95p latency jumps for small-chat routes, (2) Dedicated autoscaler flapping after burst windows. Leave notes + quick mitigations below.

Shift summary (03/12 -> 03/13):
- 00:45 UTC: minor spike on chat-short-hosted (route: /api/v1/chat) — 95p latency up from 120ms -> 490ms for ~8m. Root cause: sudden kv-cache eviction bursts on the host-group serving 'mistral-v2-small-q8' variants. Cleared by cache warmup, no further action required.
- 02:10 UTC: Dedicated pool-3 had autoscaler thrash after AWS spot reclaim in us-west-2a. One worker replaced, scaling policy attempted rapid add/remove; sustained throughput briefly degraded but no user-facing errors.
- 04:05 UTC: Embedding ingest job (embed-batch-ingest-7) retried 2x due to transient DB write timeouts; succeeded at 04:11 UTC.

Open items for next shift / reminders:
- Watch for repeated kv-cache eviction patterns. If you see 3+ eviction spikes in 30 minutes: escalate to SRE lead and consider temporary bump of in-memory kv-cache size for affected pool.
- Autoscaler: if flapping recurs, apply temporary policy: min_replicas = current_replicas, add stabilization window = 180s on scale-down. Ticket OPS-3124 tracks canonical fix.
- Embedding DB timeouts: check RDS replica lag and p99 write latency. If p99 write > 200ms, pause non-critical ingest jobs (embed-batch-ingest-*) until cleared.

Quick commands (use console role: platform-oncall):
- Tail app logs for route: $ kubectl -n hosted logs -l route=chat-short-hosted -f --since=15m
- Inspect kv-cache metrics (Prom): $ curl -sS "http://prom:9090/api/v1/query?query=kv_cache_evictions_total%7Bpool%3D'pool-3'%7D" | jq
- Temporarily increase cache limit (careful, only for 10m): $ terraform apply -var 'kv_cache_limit=6GB' -target=module.pool3.cache && alert on rollback
- Add autoscaler stabilization (K8s HPA patch): $ kubectl patch hpa dedicated-pool-3 -p '{"spec":{"behavior":{"scaleDown":{"stabilizationWindowSeconds":180}}}}'

Short runbook segments (notes-to-self style):
- kv-cache eviction storm (short-chat routes):
  symptoms: sudden 95/99 latency spikes, token generation still proceeding but with high tail latency, cpu is normal, GPU utilization unaffected.
  quick triage: look at prom metrics: kv_cache_evictions_total, kv_cache_miss_ratio, route_p95_latency. If eviction_count spikes and miss_ratio > 0.25 -> likely cache thrash.
  mitigation: 1) mark affected pool read-only for non-critical routes (console -> routing -> set policy to tie-break to other pools) 2) if urgent, bump cache limit for pool, restart workers gracefully (rolling) to restore warm cache.
  longer fix: reduce background TTLs, add jitter to eviction TTLs, and consider rate-limiter at frontend for noisy clients.

- Dedicated autoscaler flapping after spot reclaim:
  symptoms: rapid scale down/up cycles, pod restarts, transient 5xx on long-tail batch requests.
  quick triage: check cloud provider events for spot reclaim, check hpa events: $ kubectl get events -n dedicated | grep HPA
  mitigation: patch HPA stabilization window (scaleDown 180s), optionally pin some buffer capacity (reserve 1-2 on-demand nodes) until longer-term scheduling fix shipped.

Escalation contacts:
- On-call SRE (pager): Jonah Reyes (pager)
- Platform infra lead: Priya Nair (Slack dms)
- Customer-facing incidents: page duty manager (ops-dm) if > 30m degradation for production routes

Notes / things I scribbled: 
- Observed a client that issues short, repeated prefix-only requests (likely test harness) — this pattern correlates with cache churn. Add a rate limit rule for short-prefetch fingerprints.
- Consider adding a small warmup probe when new workers join so they fetch popular prefixes proactively.

Checklist for next shift:
- [ ] Verify no ongoing eviction spikes in last 60m
- [ ] Confirm dedicated pool autoscaler events are stabilized
- [ ] Make sure embed ingestion backlog is below 1k items and no DB timeouts
- [ ] Post a short note in #platform-ops summarizing events and actions taken

Notes-to-next-oncall: 
- If you get OPS-3124 re-opened, include the autoscaler event logs and node termination traces.
- If we need to bump cache sizes, coordinate with infra to watch memory pressure on nodes (don't exceed 85% host mem).

Random crumbs: 
- Helpful dashboards: "KV Cache - Pool 3" and "Dedicated Scaling - us-west-2" (console -> dashboards)
- Related PRs: #998 contains a temporary HPA stabilization change we merged as a bandaid.

End-of-shift signoff (Maya): leaving notes in ticket OPS-3124 and pinned msg in slack thread. No customer-visible incident.

---
Small personal reminder: when busy, keep notes terse. This helps handoff clarity.
